Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: L1 gold records uniformly report human oral bioavailability below 20%: tegaserod ~10% fasted (C01, C06, C18, C22), epanolol 5.85–7.89% across fasted/fed solution/tablet (C02, C04, C08, C11, C14, C21), aliskiren 2–5% (C05, C13, C17, C20), alvimopan 6% (C09, C10, C16, C19), melagatran 3–7% fasted and 0.9% fed (C07, C15), argatroban poor (C03), and CDP323 14% (C12).

L2 context reinforces the low-F direction for polar/peptidic molecules: argatroban and related peptidomimetics are not orally bioavailable due to poor enteral absorption and presystemic hepatic extraction (C25, C28, C35); aliskiren's low F is linked to intestinal P-gp efflux (C34); alvimopan is poor in dogs (C24); tegaserod remains ~10% (C27, C30).

L4 permeability records for peptide/peptidomimetic reference molecules show low intestinal permeability: DADLE P_B 2.46×10^-7 cm/s and Caco-2 AP-BL 7.80×10^-8 cm/s (C52, C59); FMLP Papp 1.3×10^-7 cm/s (C54); hexarelin Papp <1.5 to 6×10^-7 cm/s depending on formulation (C49, C51, C53, C55, C57); prodrug 1 Papp 1.80×10^-8 cm/s (C58).

L5 gut-wall/intestinal metabolism records mostly show very low absorptive permeability or efflux-dominated transport for peptide/macrocyclic references: MC-LR A-B 0.3–1.4% of loaded amount over 24 h and Papp AB 2.4×10^-8 cm/s with BA 4.0×10^-8 cm/s (C61, C63, C67, C70); DG013A A-B <1.0×10^-6 cm/s with B-A below LOQ (C62); compounds 25/26 A-B 0.28/0.16×10^-6 cm/s (C60, C64); indinavir mouse ileum <1.5% absorbed (C65).

Some L5 records show higher Caco-2 Papp for smaller drug-like molecules (saquinavir 2.25×10^-6, indinavir 2.49×10^-6, atazanavir 1.4–2.5×10^-6 cm/s; C66, C68, C71), but these are structurally unrelated to the query and are not F measurements; they do not provide affirmative evidence for query F≥20%.

The query's physicochemical profile (MW 4113 Da, TPSA 1646 Å², logD -19.4, 57 HBD, 56 HBA, 149 rotatable bonds, fully ionized) is far more extreme than any cited low-F context and coherently supports F < 20%; no affirmative evidence supports F ≥ 20%.
